rv.q: Nadia Fall's superbly acted production combines familiar delight with fresh pertinence.
Nadia Fall reinvigorates Mike Leigh's classic play with a star turn from Tamzin Outhwaite.
Tamzin Outhwaite's Beverley is mesmerising … the actress provides a masterclass in how to put other people down.
Fall’s revival revels in its sheer entertainment factor, emphasised by Peter McKintosh’s sitcom-esque living room set, and in Outhwaite has a comic lead on stellar form.
Overall, this is a classy revival of a text that has not wavered throughout the years and still remains as funny, embarrassing, and powerful as it did in the 1970s.

cn.t: Mike Leigh's 1977 satire proves surprisingly relevant in this well-received revival, with critics praising its timeless skewering of aspirational middle-class pretensions and a standout central performance that brings the monstrous Beverly vividly to life.
